label: Electrical
headline_template: Shows up when the lights don’t.
lede_template: Panels, outlets, and the stuff that sparks in {city}.

services.name: Outlets and switches
services.what: Dead outlets, a switch that doesn’t do anything, or a plug that’s loose and warm.
services.benefit: The room works again, and you stop using a power strip as a permanent fix.

services.name: Panel work
services.what: A full panel, a breaker that won’t hold, or a box that’s out of space.
services.benefit: The heart of the house can take the load without tripping all afternoon.

services.name: Lighting
services.what: A room that’s too dark, a fixture that’s dead, or cans that need to go in.
services.benefit: You can see the workbench, the kitchen, or the front step at night.

services.name: Ceiling fans
services.what: A fan that wobbles, a switch that only does one speed, or a new fan where a light is now.
services.benefit: Air moving in the room that actually needs it.

services.name: Troubleshooting
services.what: Something electrical is wrong and you don’t know which box or wire.
services.benefit: A diagnosis before you replace the wrong part.

services.name: Adds and rewires
services.what: A new circuit for a shop, EV, or kitchen, or old cloth wire that has to go.
services.benefit: The house can take the new load without a fire-hazard workaround.

process.title: You call the shop
process.body: The number on this page rings them. Say if something sparked, a breaker keeps tripping, or you need a fan or outlet added.

process.title: They tell you if they can take it
process.body: Ask if they cover your street and whether it’s a same-day look or a scheduled install.

process.title: They look, then they talk
process.body: A tech should find the fault and tell you repair vs replace before they open walls or swap a panel.

faqs.q: How do I know I need an electrician?
faqs.a: Breakers that trip, outlets that die, lights that flicker, a burning smell, or a job that needs a new circuit. If you smell burning, get out and call.

faqs.q: What should I do while I wait?
faqs.a: If something is sparking or hot, kill that breaker. Don’t keep resetting a breaker that trips twice.
